findings.suggested_fix: After closing the appointment, assert with nextOf(app, ...) (default clock: Monday 08:00 Kolkata). The closed 09:00 appointment is then still in the future, so only the status filter can exclude it.
findings.text: The Completed and No-show tests call nextOf with the 'started' clock (Monday 09:20). The closed 09:00 appointments already start before now, so the time filter hides them anyway. These tests would pass even if the SCHEDULED status filter were removed, so S-2 AC3 is not really tested.

rubric_items.reason: The new cases target S-2 AC3 (Completed, No-show) and S-5 AC3 (order), which closes the gaps left after impl. But the Completed and No-show tests do not separate the status filter from the time filter.

Assertions check observable API bodies (status, id, starts_at, ordered ids). The closed-appointment assertions are weak: the closed slots are already in the past under the 'started' clock, so these tests would pass even without the status filter.
Edge cases are covered (Completed, No-show, ordering, plus the earlier null, Cancelled, Inactive and past cases). The changed GET /api/patients endpoint has no error-path test.
Vitest and Supertest against a throwaway PostgreSQL with a fixed clock, in api/test, run by npm test, as the strategy says. Test names do not start with requirement IDs as the strategy requires.
No counts or coverage are invented. Coverage is reported as unavailable, which matches the verifier's coverage step status 'skip' (exit 78).
